Tulsa housing and where the neighborhoods sit

Tulsa is the second-largest city in Oklahoma, in the northeast corner of the state, and covers about 183 square miles of land on both sides of the Arkansas River. Downtown sits inside the inner dispersal loop formed by Interstate 244, Highway 64 and Highway 75. Midtown, with Maple Ridge, Cherry Street and Brookside, is the historic residential core. Much of the southern half of the city was built after 1970, West Tulsa lies across the river, and the north holds the airport and Mohawk Park.

The housing follows those layers: Craftsman, Tudor and Art Deco houses in the older core, ranch and Mid-Century Modern homes in the south, east and Midtown, and newer subdivisions farther out. Age drives most of the inspection questions a buyer will raise.

Which county bills a Tulsa address

Almost all of Tulsa is in Tulsa County, but small parts of the city extend into Osage and Wagoner counties, so the county on your bill depends on the parcel. Portions in Osage County are in Tulsa Public Schools. Portions in Wagoner County are served by the Tulsa, Broken Arrow and Catoosa districts.

If your house is near the edge of the city, look up the parcel on the Tulsa County Assessor's property search before assuming the county. For houses in Tulsa County, the Tulsa County Treasurer bills and collects the tax, and the Assessor sets the value.

Our Tulsa County property tax guide covers the county offices in more detail. This page stays on the city side: floods, utilities, schools, local liens and what they mean for a sale.

Flood history and what it means for a sale

Tulsa suffered serious flooding and answered with a nationally recognized plan. A comprehensive flood management effort followed the 1984 flood, which dropped about 15 inches of rain overnight, killed 14 people, injured 288 and destroyed 7,000 buildings.

In 2021 the city announced it had moved from Class 2 to Class 1 in FEMA's Community Rating System, the highest rank, with a 45% discount on National Flood Insurance Program premiums starting in April 2022. It was one of only two communities nationwide at Class 1, and the rating runs on a three-year cycle. Call the city for the current class before you quote a discount to a buyer.

  • Oklahoma's seller disclosure form asks about flood zone status, water seepage and drainage problems.
  • Gather any flood insurance declarations and elevation or repair records before listing.
  • If your house was ever flooded, tell the buyer in writing. The Tulsa County Assessor also asks owners to report damage from fire, flood or storm.

Storms, hail and summer heat

Tulsa gets just under 41 inches of rain a year, and May is the wettest month at about 5.9 inches. Severe thunderstorms with large hail, damaging winds and sometimes tornadoes are most common in spring and early summer.

Triple-digit days average about 11 a year, mostly from July to early September, so roofs and air conditioning units carry the heat and hail load. Hail is the most common homeowners claim type in Oklahoma. Ask your insurer about a separate wind or hail deductible before you decide on repairs.

School districts and your tax rate

Tulsa Public Schools is the second-largest district in Oklahoma, with nine high schools and more than 41,000 students. It is not the only one. Parts of the city in Tulsa County fall in Berryhill, Bixby, Broken Arrow, Jenks, Owasso or Union districts.

The district shows up on your tax bill, because rates are set by taxing district. Two houses with the same value can get different bills if they sit in different districts, which is worth knowing when a buyer compares properties.

Reading a Tulsa property tax bill

A Tulsa bill is built in steps: taxable value, then assessed value, then the rate for your taxing districts. The County Assessor publishes the formula and a calculator for it.

StepWhat to do
Taxable Fair Cash ValueStart with this figure from your valuation notice
Assessed Value (Gross)Multiply by 0.11
Homestead exemptionSubtract $1,000 if you qualify
TaxMultiply what is left by the rate per $1,000 for your taxing district

The Assessor's tax estimator gives a current estimate for your parcel. The Treasurer's June tax distribution mailing shows how bills are divided among the schools, cities, the City-County Library, the City-County Health Department and the county.

City charges and liens that follow the house

City cleanup and mowing charges can become part of the property tax record. Tulsa County's tax auction notice says properties are sold for unpaid property taxes or for special assessments such as cleaning and mowing. The city's nuisance abatement work covers removal of tall grass, weeds and vegetation, and city resolutions authorize the cleaning, cutting and mowing of property.

  • Drive by the property and look for notices on the door or the lot.
  • Ask the Treasurer's office at 918-596-5071 whether any special assessment sits on the parcel.
  • Pay or clear the charge at closing so it does not carry over to the buyer.

Transferring water, sewer and trash service

The City of Tulsa turns on, transfers or shuts off water, sewer and refuse service through its utility office, and a change normally takes 3 business days after the request.

Request it online, by email to Tulsa311@cityoftulsa.org, by calling 311 or (918) 596-2100 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., or in person at Utilities Customer Service, City Hall, 175 E. 2nd Street. You must be listed on the account and have your customer ID and account number. For a shutoff, give a forwarding address for the final bill. Any balance is charged against your deposit first. Buyers of properties with a prior balance may need to appear in person with a deed.

Ask for your shutoff or transfer a few days ahead of the closing date.

What to do before you list

Start with the parcel. Confirm the county, then check the Treasurer's record for any balance or special assessment. Next, read the flood zone status and gather any insurance and repair records, since the disclosure form asks about both. Last, line up your utility transfer for a few days before closing.

Sellers who do these three things before the first showing tend to have fewer delays at the title company, because the usual surprises have already come up.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends my Tulsa property tax bill?

The Tulsa County Treasurer, based on the value set by the Tulsa County Assessor. A few parcels at the edge of the city sit in Osage or Wagoner counties, which bill separately.

Is Tulsa in a flood zone?

Parts of it are. Tulsa has floodplain areas and a long flood history, and the city has earned the top rank in FEMA's Community Rating System. Check the specific parcel and ask your insurer.

How long does it take to move Tulsa utilities to a buyer?

Transfers and shutoffs normally take 3 business days after the request.

Can a city mowing charge affect my sale?

Yes. Special assessments such as cleaning and mowing can be collected through the county tax process and can lead to a tax auction if unpaid, so clear them before or at closing.

Where can I get a current Tulsa tax estimate?

Use the County Assessor's tax estimator, which applies the formula to your parcel. Rates are set by taxing district, so the result depends on which school district your house is in.
